study: Jaciw et al. 2016, iRAISE (Internet-based Reading Apprenticeship), i3 evaluation
eval_evidence: Conducted by Empirical Education Inc. under subcontract with WestEd; the report states Empirical Education 'was provided with independence in reporting' and is 'the independent evaluator of WestEd's 2012 Investing in Innovation (i3)' grant. Third-party independent eval firm.
developer_evidence: iRAISE is WestEd Strategic Literacy Institute's (SLI's) own online Reading Apprenticeship PD; SLI (the developer) ran the year-long online learning community (5-day Foundations + monthly Ignite/PLC sessions with facilitators). No separate trainer organisation; the developers delivered the PD.
cascade_evidence: SLI/WestEd staff facilitated the online sessions directly to the participating science teachers; no train-the-trainer intermediary cadre is described. Developer-to-teacher direct delivery.
counterfactual_evidence: Control = 'business as usual'; control teachers continued normal practice. Minor noted contamination: three control (and four treatment) teachers reported 1-3 days of prior 'RA training', but the assigned control condition was BAU with no alternative PD.
coaching_evidence: iRAISE is an online year-long learning community (online synchronous sessions with facilitators/peers plus asynchronous work, monthly follow-up Ignite/PLC meetings); no ongoing in-class coaching or classroom-observation visits to teachers.
student_dose_evidence: Reading Apprenticeship is a disciplinary-literacy instructional framework that changes the science teacher's regular instruction; no tutoring/pull-out/extra-minutes or student-facing software dose added.
maturity_evidence: Impact study ran in 2014-15, the first full implementation year of the online iRAISE program (SLI had only piloted it with 25 teachers in 2013-14); study teachers were new to iRAISE, with student outcomes measured at the end of that single year.
